clue.text: Unsettled question's no problem

parts.note: QU is a short form of question
something that is no problem is easy

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a query they raise is no trouble at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling queasy means having an unsettled, nauseous stomach.

clue.text: Medley of tunes — can I assume, about fifty?

indicators.note: the prison and the guess are placed about, that is around, the Roman numeral

parts.note: can and quod are both slang words for prison
saying I bet is a casual way of saying I assume or I suppose
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A musician wonders whether a medley might run to about fifty tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb (am I able) but is British slang for prison; 'about' wraps the prison word and the guess round the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A quodlibet is a musical piece combining several familiar tunes, a kind of medley.

clue.text: Keep some content in Surrey town

indicators.note: the letters are the content held in the words keep some

explanation.surface: A request to keep a little of something inside a town in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: EPSOM is a Surrey town, famous for the Derby horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is a market town in the English county of Surrey.

clue.text: From close inspection, said salary's peanuts

indicators.note: said tells us the phrase is spoken and the spelling follows its sound

parts.note: screw is British slang for wages, and peanuts means tiny, so the pay is a tiny screw

explanation.surface: A complaint, after a close inspection, that the salary on offer is a pittance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' is old British slang for a wage; 'peanuts' means a tiny amount, so 'screw tiny' spoken aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrutiny is a careful, searching examination, which is what close inspection means.

clue.text: Refrains from boring tasks going round America

indicators.note: the household jobs go round, so they surround the country's abbreviation

parts.note: chores are dull routine jobs

explanation.surface: Someone abstains from tedious jobs while touring the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrains' looks like a verb (holds back) but is the noun: repeated parts of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorus is the repeated section of a song, also called a refrain.

clue.text: Port Authority providing shelter when her mast is damaged outside

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit outside, wrapping round the word for shelter
something damaged is broken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
an arbour is a leafy shady shelter in a garden

explanation.surface: A port official offers refuge to a boat whose mast has been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is damaged' rearranges the boat's 'her mast'; 'outside' wraps that round the garden shelter. 'providing' and 'when' are only link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbourmaster is the official in authority over a port, so a person in charge of a port is a fitting definition.

clue.text: Thugs responsible for town's two leaders being knocked off

indicators.note: the first two letters of the word are removed, like leaders knocked off the front

parts.note: a borough is a town, and town's read as plural gives boroughs

explanation.surface: Gangsters blamed for the murder of a town's top two officials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'town's' is read as 'towns' in the plural, BOROUGHS. 'responsible for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughs is an old-fashioned word for violent, rowdy men, the same sense as thugs.

clue.text: Southern religious observance

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south or southern
pi is short for pious, meaning religious
a ritual is a ceremonial religious observance

explanation.surface: A description of religious practice in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (pious) is a crossword convention for 'religious'. The whole clue also defines: spirituals are religious songs from the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiritual is a religious folk song first sung by Black communities in the American South.

clue.text: Soundly upset Arab leader

indicators.note: soundly tells us to go by how the word is spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: to upset someone is to shake them

explanation.surface: An Arab chief has been thoroughly overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like it means 'thoroughly'. This works with the pronunciation 'shake'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheik is the chief of an Arab tribe or family, so an Arab leader.

clue.text: Keep watch

definitions.meaning: to keep a rule or a festival is to follow it
to watch is to look at closely

explanation.definitionFit: Observe means both to keep a law or custom and to watch carefully.

clue.text: The man is blest, being incorporated in this

definitions.text: The man is blest, being incorporated in this

indicators.note: letters incorporated are made into one new body, so they are formed into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A blessed man taken into the heart of some institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being incorporated' rearranges THE MAN IS BLEST. Read whole, the clue describes the ruling elite that absorbs a favoured, blessed man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Establishment is the ruling group that takes in and rewards favoured insiders.

clue.text: As a rule, rake in the dosh? On the contrary

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
on the contrary swaps the roles, so the money goes inside the rake, not the rake inside the money

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man, a roué
tin and dosh are both British slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone earning a lot of money as a habit, then reversing the claim.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'rake in' as earning money; 'in' and 'On the contrary' swap who holds whom, so the money sits inside the rake. 'Dosh' is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done as a rule is the routine, the normal regular practice.

clue.text: Having landed, I am kept within boundary

indicators.note: one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: lit is a past tense of light, meaning landed or settled on
I'm is the short form of I am

explanation.surface: An air traveller who has landed finds themselves held at the border.
explanation.walkthrough: LIT here is the past tense of 'light' in the sense 'come down and settle', as a bird lights on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a boundary or edge that marks how far something can go.

clue.text: It takes pressure to break excessively chunky little bit of wood

parts.note: too means excessively

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the word, splitting it in two

parts.note: chunky means thick
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Something too bulky needs force before it can be snapped.
explanation.walkthrough: P breaks THICK into TH and ICK. 'It takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothpick is a little sliver of wood used to clean between the teeth.

clue.text: Where to find convicts and tapsters

definitions.meaning: prisoners are found locked in cells
tapsters serve drinks, standing at the pub counter

explanation.definitionFit: Behind bars means in prison, and bar staff literally stand behind the bars they serve at.

clue.text: Horse given a further bridle

parts.note: a hack is a horse for ordinary riding
more means further or additional

explanation.surface: A horse is fitted with extra harness.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackamore is a bitless bridle used mainly to train horses.

clue.text: This provides light to cry about

indicators.note: about tells us the word turns round to read backwards

parts.note: to blub is to cry

explanation.surface: A lamp offers illumination to weep by.
explanation.definitionFit: A light bulb is the glass globe that gives out light in a lamp.

clue.text: To show disapproval of small cake, said "It keeps coming back"

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in disapproval

indicators.note: said tells us the word for the cake is spoken and spelt by its sound

parts.note: a meringue is a small light cake of whipped egg white and sugar

explanation.surface: Someone jeers at a small pastry and remarks on its tendency to return.
explanation.definitionFit: A boomerang is a curved throwing stick built to return to the person who threw it.

clue.text: Competent girl comes in early, winning

indicators.note: the girl's name comes inside near the start of the other word

parts.note: able means competent
Dora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A capable young woman arrives at work early and does well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes in early' sets the girl's name inside, just after the first letter. 'winning' is the adjective meaning charming, not winning a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning used as an adjective means charming or appealing, which is what adorable means.

clue.text: Minute parasite

definitions.meaning: a moment or very short time, as in 'just a minute'
a small blood-sucking creature like a mite

explanation.definitionFit: A tick is both a moment (just a tick) and a blood-sucking parasite related to mites.

clue.text: Writer getting older — plain ugly

indicators.note: an ugly arrangement is a disordered one, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author grows older and less attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: Luigi Pirandello was an Italian playwright and novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Pirandello was a Nobel-winning Italian dramatist and novelist.

clue.text: Like a seabird, following behind vessel

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A gull trailing behind a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern means at or towards the back of a ship, behind the vessel.

clue.text: A truism — there's no more to be said

definitions.meaning: a statement so obvious it says only that a thing is itself

definitions.text: there's no more to be said

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase states a tautology and is also a set expression ending a matter.

clue.text: Toledo's first sword found in a tent

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: an épée is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: A Toledo blade turns up inside a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: Toledo in Spain is famous for its swords, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepee is a cone-shaped tent of the Plains peoples of North America.

clue.text: Light entertainment — critical assessment is broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard on air, so we go by the spoken sound

parts.note: a review is a critical assessment

explanation.surface: A theatre critic's verdict on a light show goes out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a light theatrical show of sketches, songs and dances.

clue.text: Outspoken, very often coming across like leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of each word before it

explanation.surface: Someone frank who tends to come over as a born leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Vocal describes someone who speaks out freely and forcefully, which outspoken also means.

clue.text: A protected species, shrub is cut back by earth mother

indicators.note: the shrub's back end is cut off, losing its final letter

parts.note: a protea is a South African flowering shrub
Ge, or Gaia, is the Greek goddess of the earth, mother of the Titans

explanation.surface: A conservation note about pruning a rare shrub near a nature goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A protected species' looks like it describes an endangered plant; it is a jokey way to say a protected kind of person.
explanation.definitionFit: A protégé is a person under the protection and guidance of a patron, a protected kind of person.

clue.text: Novel about leader's old violin

parts.note: a rebec is a medieval bowed instrument, and leader's says it leads, coming first
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A book about a bandleader's antique fiddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebecca' is Daphne du Maurier's novel. 'leader's' places REBEC first, ahead of CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca is a famous 1938 novel by Daphne du Maurier.

clue.text: Hereafter tiny tree develops

indicators.note: something that develops changes form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: From now on, a little sapling grows.
explanation.definitionFit: The hereafter is life after death, often pictured as eternity.

clue.text: Let loose in a bender, feeling of disorientation (3,3) 22,912

indicators.note: in places the jumbled word inside the other

parts.note: a jag is a drinking spree, a bender

indicators.note: let loose means set free and scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lets themselves go on a drinking binge and ends up dazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges 'Let', and 'in' sets the result inside a slang word for a drinking spree.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet lag is the tiredness and disorientation felt after flying across time zones.
